svg.text: Pump sensing — low-side shunts, Kelvin pairs to four INA226s
P1–P3 on the always-on bus; P4's feed is open. The negative lead carries every operating mode, so one shunt per pump sees them all.
publishes volts and amps to Signal K
Each Kelvin lead of an external shunt is fused at the shunt end: an open return downstream would otherwise send motor current down the lead.
A tripped breaker or blown fuse reads as zero volts on that pump's VBUS — an alarm.
P1, P2 and P4 current never crosses the board; P3's already does, through Q8.
10 kΩ series resistor and 0.5 A sense-lead fuses are stand-ins.
